title: Customer Success Playbook: Customer Reference Program (Reference Readiness + Ongoing Outcomes)
author: Rachel Kim
body:
## Purpose
This playbook helps Customer Success (CS) consistently identify, qualify, and operationalize customers who can participate in Redwood Inference’s Customer Reference Program.

The program has two customer-facing motions:
1) **Public case study participation** (web + PDF, approved quotes, approved metrics)
2) **Reference calls** (scheduled conversations with qualified prospects)

CS is responsible for ensuring customers are **reference-ready** (stable production usage, clear outcomes, defined guardrails, and a prepared champion) and that we can **collect outcomes over time** to keep stories current.

This page is customer-sensitive. Do not copy/paste externally.

---

## Definitions
- **Design partner (for this program):** A customer willing to participate in public case study content and/or be available for periodic reference calls.
- **Reference-ready:** Customer meets minimum stability, satisfaction, and champion criteria; legal/comms path is known; CS can support the workload without creating customer burden.
- **Champion:** Primary internal advocate who can speak credibly about outcomes and participate in approvals.
- **Spokesperson:** The approved individual(s) who can be quoted and/or join reference calls.
- **Outcomes:** Quantified improvements and operational wins (e.g., latency p95, error rate, cost/token, throughput, uptime, deployment compliance posture) tied to a clear measurement window.

---

## When to use this playbook
Use this playbook when:
- A customer is being considered for a case study or reference calls.
- Sales requests a reference for a live deal.
- A customer is entering/has entered stable production and we want to capture measurable wins for QBRs.
- Marketing is scheduling case study interviews and needs CS support for readiness + validation.

---

## CS goals and success criteria
### CS goals
- Protect the customer experience (no surprises, no undue burden, clear boundaries).
- Ensure references are credible (stable usage, validated outcomes, repeatable narrative).
- Make reference participation predictable for Sales (routing, SLAs, follow-through).
- Keep stories current (quarterly outcomes refresh, incident notes, deployment changes).

### Success criteria (CS-owned)
- Reference candidates are screened with the checklist below and have an assigned CS owner.
- Champion/spokesperson is confirmed and trained on reference call boundaries.
- Outcome metrics are captured with a measurement note (source + window + caveats).
- Customer has a clear opt-out path and can control frequency.

---

## Roles and responsibilities (CS-centric view)
**CSM (Account owner)**
- Owns the customer relationship and readiness decision.
- Secures customer consent for participation type(s) and sets expectations.
- Collects outcomes for QBR and routes metrics validation requests.

**Sr CSM / Reference Program CS lead (Miguel Santos)**
- Coach CSMs on readiness, boundaries, and de-risking.
- Escalation point for reference call conflicts or customer fatigue.

**Solutions Engineering (SE)**
- Validates technical architecture and measurement methodology.
- Attends reference calls when technical depth is needed.

**Marketing (Program owner + writer)**
- Drives case study production, interviewing, drafting, and publishing.
- Maintains approved messaging framework.

**Legal**
- Owns release language, approvals, and any NDA/MSA constraints.

**Sales (AE)**
- Submits reference requests with qualified context and desired outcomes.
- Owns prospect management and follow-up.

---

## Reference readiness criteria (CS checklist)
A customer is generally reference-ready when they meet **all** “Must-have” criteria and at least **two** “Strong signals”. If any “Do not proceed” flags apply, pause and escalate.

### Must-have
1) **Production usage is stable**
   - In production (or production-like steady state) for >= 4 weeks OR has completed a defined POC with clear acceptance criteria.
   - No ongoing Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents attributable to Redwood in the last 14 days.
   - Known steady-state traffic pattern (peak hours, seasonality, burst behavior).

2) **Customer sentiment is positive**
   - CSM confidence: customer is satisfied and would recommend Redwood.
   - Open escalations are managed with a committed remediation plan.

3) **A champion exists and is responsive**
   - Champion can articulate “why Redwood” and describe outcomes.
   - Champion can route approvals internally (comms, legal, leadership).

4) **Participation type and boundaries are explicit**
   - Reference-call-only vs public case study is confirmed.
   - Topics to avoid are documented (security, vendors, workload specifics, regulated data, procurement).

### Strong signals
- Customer has a measurable win tied to production economics (latency, cost/token, throughput).
- Customer is using Dedicated or Private with a clear compliance/security story (audit logs, KMS, isolation).
- Customer has a repeatable use case with broad relevance (support agent, doc search, fintech risk, dev tools).
- Customer is already speaking publicly (conference talk, blog) about LLM use (even if not about Redwood).

### Do not proceed (pause + escalate)
- Customer is in an active escalation or has unresolved trust issues.
- Legal/comms has explicitly blocked any external references.
- Customer’s metrics are not verifiable or would require exposing sensitive workload details.
- Customer team is changing ownership (champion leaving, re-org) and consent is uncertain.

---

## Reference participation tiers (set expectations early)
Offer customers a tiered menu. Do not “upsell” tiers; allow customers to choose the lowest-friction option.

**Tier 1 — Reference call only (low lift)**
- 1–2 calls per quarter maximum
- 30 minutes each
- Pre-brief provided by Redwood
- Customer can decline any request

**Tier 2 — Quote + logo (medium lift)**
- Written quotes (pre-approved)
- Logo usage in case study page, decks, and marketplace assets (as approved)
- No architecture diagram unless explicitly approved

**Tier 3 — Full case study (high lift)**
- 1–2 interviews (business + technical)
- Customer review + redlines
- Optional architecture diagram
- Outcome metrics included with defined measurement windows

CS guidance: If a customer is hesitant, start at Tier 1. Many customers convert to Tier 2/3 after one positive reference experience.

---

## CS workflow: from candidate to “reference-ready”
### Step 1 — Identify candidates (signals)
Where candidates come from:
- QBR outcomes and expansions
- Dedicated/Private go-lives
- High NPS moments / customer praise
- Successful incident response recovery (handled well, trust strengthened)
- SE identifies a uniquely strong architecture story

CS actions:
- Add candidate to the internal tracker (or ask Marketing Ops to add) and note deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
- Draft 2–3 candidate outcomes (even if placeholders) and where the data likely lives.

### Step 2 — Validate baseline and outcomes (with SE as needed)
Minimum outcome artifacts (internal):
- **Metric name** (e.g., p95 latency, cost/token, error rate)
- **Before** and **after** values (or baseline vs Redwood) OR a defensible qualitative outcome if numbers are blocked
- **Window** (dates, sample size, steady-state conditions)
- **Source** (Console dashboard, customer telemetry, benchmark harness)
- **Caveats** (workload shape, prompt set, model version)

Rules:
- Do not publish “up to” claims without a clear range and caveat.
- If customer provides numbers, confirm that they are comfortable with the unit and context.

### Step 3 — Confirm champion/spokesperson and approvals path
CS questions to resolve:
- Who is the primary champion?
- Who is the named spokesperson (title + team)?
- Who must approve externally (Legal, Comms/PR, Security, Exec sponsor)?
- Is there a preferred timeline or blackout period?

### Step 4 — Set reference boundaries and customer experience
Before any reference call, confirm:
- Allowed topics (OK): latency/cost/reliability improvements, integration process, why Dedicated/Private, general architecture patterns
- Avoid topics (not OK): exact traffic volumes, sensitive vendor lists, security findings, regulated data specifics, pricing/contract terms, internal roadmap commitments
- Frequency limit and preferred times
- Whether calls must be recorded (default: **no**)

### Step 5 — Mark as reference-ready + maintain
Once ready:
- Ensure the account has an internal “reference readiness” status set (per CRM standards).
- Store internal one-pager and keep it updated after each reference event.

---

## Reference call operations (CS responsibilities)
### Intake requirements (what Sales must provide)
CS should not schedule a reference call without:
- Prospect company + industry + stage (evaluation/POC/procurement)
- What they are trying to validate (e.g., Dedicated latency predictability, Private compliance)
- Target date range + urgency
- Topics the prospect will ask about
- SE attendance request (yes/no) and why

If missing, route back to AE with a single question: “What decision will this call unlock?”

### CS SLAs
- Acknowledge internal request: **1 business day**
- Provide candidate reference options OR decline with reason: **2 business days**
- Target scheduling lead time: **5–7 business days** (faster only with customer opt-in)

### Customer prep (CS-owned)
Send the customer a short prep note (email) that includes:
- Who the prospect is (high level)
- Purpose of the call
- Confirmed time and duration
- Topics to focus on + topics to avoid
- Who from Redwood will attend
- Reminder that they can redirect or decline any question

### Redwood internal prep (CS-owned, with AE/SE)
- Align on 3–5 key points (the “story spine”)
- Confirm what metrics are safe to repeat verbally
- Decide who will open/close, and how to handle security questions
- Prepare a “parking lot” path: “We can follow up offline with SE / security documentation”

### During the call
CS is the moderator:
- Open with boundaries and agenda
- Keep the customer from being interrogated; move to outcomes and implementation quickly
- Timebox (leave 5 minutes for wrap-up)

### Post-call follow-up (CS-owned)
Within 1 business day:
- Thank the customer and confirm whether any follow-up is needed
- Capture outcomes discussed and any new claims/questions
- Note customer sentiment (energized/neutral/fatigued)
- Update reference readiness and future availability

---

## Ongoing outcomes collection (for QBRs and story freshness)
### What to capture (quarterly, lightweight)
CS should aim to refresh outcomes once per quarter for reference customers:
- **Performance:** latency p50/p95, time-to-first-token (if relevant), throughput
- **Reliability:** error rates, incident frequency/severity, fallback/routing effectiveness
- **Economics:** cost/token, cost/query, cache hit rate, batching efficiency
- **Operational wins:** rollout safety (canary/fallback), debugging time reduction, audit log usage, compliance posture

### How to capture without customer burden
Preferred order of sources:
1) Redwood Console screenshots/exports (customer-approved)
2) Redwood internal telemetry summaries (aggregated)
3) Customer-provided dashboards (only if already available)
4) Controlled benchmark run (SE-owned) using an agreed prompt set

Guidance:
- Do not ask for raw logs or anything that triggers a security review unless necessary.
- Use a consistent measurement window (e.g., last 14 days steady-state) and document exceptions.

### Metric hygiene rules (minimum standard)
When recording a metric for future use, include:
- Exact definition (e.g., “p95 end-to-end latency, excluding client-side retries”)
- Model name/version and deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- Region (if relevant)
- Traffic characteristics (avg input tokens, output tokens, streaming vs non-streaming)
- Any major changes since prior quarter (model swap, quantization, routing policy)

---

## Customer communication templates (CS)
### Template A — Invitation to be a reference (reference-call-only)
Subject: Quick ask: occasional reference call for Redwood?

Hi {{Name}},

You’ve been a strong partner as you’ve brought {{use case}} into production. We’re building a small customer reference group to help other engineering teams understand what “good” production inference looks like (latency, reliability, and deployment patterns).

Would you be open to being available for up to **1–2 short reference calls per quarter**, with full control over timing and topics? We’ll always send a brief ahead of time, and you can decline any request.

If you’re open to it, I’ll confirm your preferred boundaries (topics to avoid, best scheduling windows) and who should be the primary spokesperson.

Thanks,
{{CSM name}}

### Template B — Setting boundaries before a reference call
Subject: Reference call prep: {{Prospect}} on {{Date}}

Hi {{Name}},

Thanks again for helping with this reference call. Here are the guardrails we’ll follow:
- Goal: help {{Prospect}} understand your experience with Redwood for {{use case}}.
- OK topics: integration approach, reliability/operations, general outcomes (latency/cost/reliability), why you chose {{Hosted/Dedicated/Private}}.
- Please avoid: exact volumes, pricing/contract details, vendor evaluations, security findings, anything about regulated data specifics.

Agenda (30 min): 5 min context, 20 min discussion, 5 min wrap-up.

If any question feels uncomfortable, feel free to redirect and I’ll step in.

Best,
{{CSM name}}

---

## Common risks and how CS mitigates them
### Risk: Customer fatigue (“too many calls”)
Mitigations:
- Set a hard frequency cap per quarter
- Rotate references when possible
- Offer async alternatives (written Q&A) when appropriate
- Always confirm availability; never assume

### Risk: Unverifiable or misleading metrics
Mitigations:
- Require measurement window + source + caveats
- Run metrics through SE validation when technical
- Avoid grand claims; prefer “in our workload” phrasing

### Risk: Security/compliance sensitivities
Mitigations:
- Pre-approve allowed topics
- Route security deep questions to Redwood security documentation and SE follow-up
- Keep architecture diagrams abstract unless approved

### Risk: Sales-prospect mismatch (wrong reference for the deal)
Mitigations:
- Require intake details (decision to unlock)
- Match by deployment mode + industry constraints
- Decline quickly if mismatch to avoid wasting customer goodwill

---

## Escalation and decision policy
Escalate to the Sr CSM / CS leadership when:
- The customer has had a Sev-1/Sev-2 incident in the last 14 days.
- The AE requests an urgent call (< 72 hours) and customer hasn’t agreed to that pace.
- The prospect is a direct competitor of the reference customer.
- The call includes procurement/pricing pressure (not appropriate for references).

CS can decline a reference request if it risks customer trust. Provide Sales with:
- a short reason (“timing”, “fatigue”, “topic mismatch”), and
- the next best option (different reference, SE call, or documentation).

---

## What “good” looks like (examples)
The following are examples of acceptable, defensible outcome framing:
- “In our production workload, p95 latency decreased from ~X ms to ~Y ms after moving to Dedicated capacity, with a defined measurement window and steady traffic profile.”
- “We reduced cost per query by ~N% after implementing caching and batching recommendations, measured over two weeks of steady-state traffic.”
- “Private deployment met our network isolation and audit logging requirements; we integrated customer-managed keys via KMS.”

Avoid:
- “2x faster for everyone” (too broad)
- “Zero downtime” (rarely defensible)
- “Guaranteed” language unless aligned to current SLA terms

---

## Operational checklist (copy/paste)
**Reference readiness checklist (CSM):**
- [ ] Stable production/POC outcome confirmed
- [ ] Customer sentiment positive; no active escalations
- [ ] Champion + spokesperson identified
- [ ] Participation tier agreed (Tier 1/2/3)
- [ ] Approval path known (Legal/Comms/Security)
- [ ] Guardrails documented (OK/avoid topics)
- [ ] Outcomes captured with sources + window + caveats
- [ ] Reference availability windows recorded

**Reference call checklist (per request):**
- [ ] AE provided intake details (decision to unlock)
- [ ] Customer availability confirmed
- [ ] Internal prep completed (talk track + SE attendance)
- [ ] Customer prep email sent
- [ ] Post-call follow-up sent + notes captured
